mappings.note: Tests what kind of question a learner should pose (how does it work, why does it happen), which is the posing-questions strand of CG-SCI2. Not C-SCI2.1, because nothing here is investigated or recorded; only the question itself is at stake.

The point of the item is that understanding comes from doing activities and experiments outside the book, i.e. conducting simple investigations. Kept at competency level rather than C-SCI2.1-LO-1, which is tied to the specific flower-extract indicator investigation.

The answer is responsibility towards nature and society, which is the sensitivity and values goal. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, which asks for concrete acts such as planting trees or reducing pollutants; this item only tests the attitude.

Physics, chemistry and biology as interconnected is exactly the unified nature of scientific knowledge named in CG-SCI1. No competency under it fits; C-SCI1.1 and C-SCI1.2 are about sorting materials and organisms.

Sour fruits and haldi stains are everyday acidity, the day-to-day application named in the outcome. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-2, because no classification of materials is asked for, only the everyday phenomenon.

Separating metals from non-metals by whether the lamp glows is differentiating conductors from insulators, the electrical twin of the heat example in LO-1. Chosen over LO-2 because the item splits two groups on one property rather than building a classification.

Sorting melting ice, ripening fruit and a dead battery into reversible and irreversible is the physical-and-chemical-change classification named explicitly in LO-2. Not LO-1, which differentiates materials, not changes.

Heat flow driving evaporation, rain and seepage is a mode of heat transfer explained as a process, which LO-2 names. Not LO-1, since the item does not ask for the cause of a single phenomenon but for the process the heat drives.

Eating, breathing and circulation as processes needed for survival sits under relating and explaining processes. Left at competency level because no learning outcome in this frame covers animal life processes: LO-3 names respiration only as a word equation, which this item does not ask for.

Plant nutrition and gas exchange as processes; same competency as the animal-life-process item because the frame offers exactly one fitting home for life processes. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-3, which is about writing word equations for photosynthesis and respiration, a skill this item never touches.

The clock as an instrument for measuring the passage of time maps to measuring quantities including time. Not C-SCI2.2, because nothing is being explained; an instrument of measurement is the whole answer.

Telling time by a shadow is answered by the phenomenon of shadow formation by light, which LO-2 covers as explaining a phenomenon. Not C-SCI2.3-LO-1, because the item asks which phenomenon the practice depends on, not how time is measured.
Solar and lunar eclipses as shadows cast by Earth and Moon is a phenomenon whose mechanism is the answer. Not LO-1, which relates a phenomenon to a causal variable such as wind speed to air pressure.

Day and night traced back to the Earth spinning on its axis is precisely relating a phenomenon to its cause. Chosen over LO-2 because the item names a cause rather than asking for the process to be described.

Science as an evolving, curiosity-driven process rather than fixed facts is the nature-of-scientific-knowledge goal. No competency under CG-SCI1 fits; both concern classifying materials and organisms.

Activity 1.1 asks students to invent questions that would lead to a given answer, which is the posing-questions strand of CG-SCI2. Not C-SCI4.2-LO-1, whose creativity is in designing and planning with available resources, not in framing questions.

The butterfly and paper plane stand for learning taking flight under curiosity, i.e. scientific temper. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-2, because this item reads the analogy rather than recounting the discovery story behind flight.

Seeing the links between human action, nature and society and using science to address them is environmental sensitivity. Kept at goal level rather than C-SCI4.1-LO-1, which demands concrete protective acts.

The expected answer is questioning, experimenting and exploring, i.e. conducting simple investigations. Not CG-SCI2 as a whole, because experimenting is the operative half of the answer and C-SCI2.1 is the more specific code that carries it.
A paper plane as the toy that inspired real explorations of flight is a story of scientific discovery. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, because no model is built or its working explained here.

Answer is responsibility towards the natural world and society. Shares the goal with the other two responsibility items because the frame offers only this one home for the values strand; C-SCI4.1-LO-1 and C-SCI4.2-LO-2 name actions and classroom conduct instead.
One-word test of whether the disciplines are separate or interconnected, i.e. the unified nature of scientific knowledge. Not CG-SCI2, since no process skill is exercised.

Naming sour fruit or a haldi stain as an everyday material question is the day-to-day acidity application. Not C-SCI2.1-LO-1, which would require the student to run the indicator investigation rather than recall the question.

The water cycle driven by the Sun heating the seas is a process to be explained, with heat as the driver. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, whose water example is depletion of the water table by human activity, which this item does not touch.

Breathing or circulation as an essential animal life process; grouped with the other life-process recall items because the frame has no learning outcome for animal life processes at all. A factual-recall cluster sharing the only outcome that fits.
Whether plants need food to grow is a life-process fact, the same competency for the same reason: no outcome under it covers plant nutrition unless word equations are demanded, which they are not.

The sundial as the ancient way of measuring time maps to measuring quantities including time. Unlike the shadow-and-light item, here the answer is the measuring method itself, so measurement beats C-SCI2.2-LO-2.

Asks what the process of science is: curiosity, questioning, openness to the unknown. That is scientific temper and the nature of scientific knowledge. Not CG-SCI2, which is about exercising the named process skills rather than describing the enterprise.

Three marks for explaining that learning happens through hands-on activity and experiment beyond the classroom, which is C-SCI2.1. Not CG-SCI3, because nothing is constructed or applied to daily life here.
Explains why the disciplines are treated as one unified endeavour, discoveries in one sparking another. That is the unified and developmental nature of scientific knowledge in CG-SCI1.

Links human activity, its impact and responsible action for sustainability, the environmental-sensitivity goal. Not C-SCI4.1, because the item asks the student to articulate the connection rather than make an effort to protect anything.

Five-mark item: the analogy is about curiosity driving learning (CG-SCI1), and its second half turns on the paper plane having inspired real flight, a discovery story (C-SCI3.1-LO-2). Both are genuinely assessed, unlike the one-mark version which only reads the analogy.

Asks how the previewed topics are linked to one another, which is the unified character of scientific knowledge. Not any single content outcome, since the item spans materials, heat, life processes and astronomy at once.
